clue.text: Very cheerful

explanation.surface: A bare description of someone in high spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: In British speech the word is an intensifier (a ripping good time, 'very good') and also means merry or high-spirited.

clue.text: A game bungler, a fussy eater

parts.note: jacks is a children's game of tossing small pieces
prat is British slang for an idiot or fool

explanation.surface: A clumsy player who is also picky about food.
explanation.walkthrough: In the nursery rhyme Jack Sprat could eat no fat.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhyme's character would eat no fat, a famously picky diner.

clue.text: "Punctual' — a term conveying "in time"

indicators.note: conveying means the quoted words carry the answer within them

explanation.surface: A note on the word punctual and what it means.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conveying' signals letters running across 'punctuaL A TERm'.
explanation.definitionFit: In time means eventually, at some point afterwards.

clue.text: Boat takes foreign money around the peninsula

indicators.note: around says the currency wraps round the boat

parts.note: the yuan is the Chinese currency
cat is short for catamaran

explanation.surface: A vessel carrying foreign cash around a coastline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' is the container signal, with the currency outside; 'takes' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Yucatan is the Mexican peninsula between the Gulf and the Caribbean.

clue.text: Bowdlerise book about rabbits without craft

indicators.note: without tells us the vessel is taken out of the novel's title

parts.note: Watership Down is Richard Adams's novel about a warren of rabbits
a ship is a craft, a vessel

explanation.surface: Someone censors a children's novel about rabbits, cutting the boats out of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes SHIP from WATERSHIP DOWN, leaving the phrase that means to dilute or soften.
explanation.definitionFit: To bowdlerise is to censor a text, making it milder, which is to dilute it.

clue.text: It's important for singer to be audible

indicators.note: to be audible says the word for singer is heard, giving one of the same sound

parts.note: waits were street singers of carols at Christmas

explanation.surface: A remark that a singer must be heard.
explanation.walkthrough: Waits are a British tradition of carol singers; WAIT said out loud gives the answer. The definition is a noun phrase: weight is a thing that matters.
explanation.definitionFit: Weight is significance or influence, something that counts.

clue.text: Old Harry makes those in authority accept two measures

indicators.note: accept means the powers take the measures into themselves

parts.note: they is the vague word for the powers that be
en and em are printers' measures of width
em is the second of the printers' measures

explanation.surface: The devil gets officials to agree to a pair of measures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accept' is the container signal. Old Harry is an old British nickname for the Devil.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Harry and the Enemy are both old names for the Devil.

clue.text: Poser — it is resolved by a quick answer

indicators.note: is resolved means the puzzling letters are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: A difficult question gets settled by a swift reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is resolved' rearranges POSER and IT; 'by' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A riposte is a quick sharp reply, a retort.

clue.text: Split personalities are not agreed

explanation.surface: A remark on psychology and disagreement.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with a divided self is cryptically not unified in thought, and the phrase means united in opinion.

clue.text: What's required in works, by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the word is heard, matching another

parts.note: kneads means works dough with the hands

explanation.surface: Asking what a factory requires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works' looks like a factory but is a verb, KNEADS; 'in' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Needs are requirements, the things that are necessary.

clue.text: Question how a place of learning is part of the church

indicators.note: part of says the college phrase sits inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE stands for the Church of England
a tech is a technical college
taken as written

explanation.surface: Asking how a college can be counted as part of the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of' is the container signal: the college phrase sits inside the Church of England's abbreviation; 'how' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To catechise is to quiz someone closely, originally on religious doctrine.

clue.text: Experts talking in plain language

indicators.note: talking says the word for experts is spoken, giving a word with the same sound

parts.note: pros, short for professionals, are experts

explanation.surface: Specialists who speak in simple, everyday words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'talking' signals that PROS, said out loud, gives a word sounding the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinary writing without verse or ornament is called prose.

clue.text: Take a walk — or will you need some traction?

explanation.surface: Advice to go for a walk, or else end up in hospital traction.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to go for a stroll, and cryptically traction in hospital would literally stretch your limbs.

clue.text: Withdraw, moving in a trance

indicators.note: moving says the letters of trance are shifted about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone retracts a statement while sleepwalking in a trance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges TRANCE; 'in a' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: To recant is to take back a statement or belief publicly.

clue.text: 12 dismount

explanation.surface: A cross-reference followed by getting off a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both to back down from a position, as 12 across does, and literally to get down off something.

clue.text: Heartlessly threatening and being obstructive

indicators.note: Heartlessly says the central letter of the word for threatening is removed

parts.note: something impending is threatening, about to happen

explanation.surface: A menacing and obstructive person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartlessly' takes the middle N out of IMPENDING.
explanation.definitionFit: Impeding means hindering or getting in the way, which is being obstructive.

clue.text: Incendiary device beginning to' generate smoke and flame

indicators.note: beginning to picks the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: reek is an old and Scottish word for smoke
fire is flame

explanation.surface: A firebomb that starts by producing smoke and flame.
explanation.walkthrough: REEK for smoke is a dialect sense the solver may not know.
explanation.definitionFit: Greek fire was a Byzantine weapon, a burning liquid used in naval warfare.

clue.text: Money intended to cover North and South

indicators.note: to cover says the fiance wraps around the letter for North

parts.note: one's intended is one's fiance

explanation.surface: Funds meant to stretch across the whole country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cover' puts N inside FIANCE, then S follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's or body's finances are their funds or money resources.

clue.text: Trouble with a car or aeroplane part

explanation.surface: A problem affecting a car or a component of an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: A tail skid is a car's rear sliding out, and also the runner under the tail of early aircraft.

clue.text: Still in 2, the French

indicators.note: in says the French article is placed within the other word

parts.note: the answer to 2 down means afterwards, as since does
le is the French masculine word for the

explanation.surface: A cross-reference with a French article, read as instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue leans on 2 down, whose answer means afterwards; 'in' is the container signal for the French article.
explanation.definitionFit: To still is to quieten, which is to silence.

clue.text: Cows — they are about 550 light

indicators.note: about says the old word for cows goes round the numeral

parts.note: kine is an old plural of cow
DL is 550 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Cattle somehow linked to a figure of 550 and light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal; 'they are' only links. Kine is an archaic plural of cow.
explanation.definitionFit: To light a fire is to kindle it, set it burning.

clue.text: Ask where choristers might be.

explanation.surface: A question about where the singers are.
explanation.definitionFit: To inquire is to ask; quire is an old spelling of choir, so singers are in quire.

clue.text: King Lear

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's tragic monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward is the name of several English monarchs and the first name of the nonsense poet Lear.

clue.text: Unseemly, squabble with bank due to hash

indicators.note: Unseemly suggests the following letters behave badly and fall into disorder

explanation.surface: An undignified row with the bank about a debt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unseemly' rearranges SQUABBLE, BANK and DUE; 'with' and 'to' link. Bubble and squeak is British fried leftover cabbage and potato.
explanation.definitionFit: Bubble and squeak is fried leftovers, a kind of hash dish.

clue.text: Simple ones in vehicle that's overturned

indicators.note: overturned means the whole construction is turned backwards in this down entry
in says the ones are placed within the vehicle

parts.note: a cab is a vehicle, a taxi
I's, plural of the Roman one

explanation.surface: Simple items inside a car that has flipped over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal, and 'overturned' turns the whole result, CISAB, backwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Basic means elementary, plain and fundamental.

clue.text: George Eliot really a woman, with opponents

parts.note: Eva is a woman's name
North and South are partners against East and West at bridge, so opponents

explanation.surface: The novelist was really female and had critics.
explanation.walkthrough: George Eliot's real name was Mary Ann Evans; 'with' links.
explanation.definitionFit: The novelist's pen name hid her birth surname, Evans.

clue.text: Kiss and cuddle one involved with elopement

explanation.surface: Romance and running off with a lover.
explanation.definitionFit: To spoon is old slang for courting caresses, and in the nursery rhyme the dish ran away with the cutlery item.

clue.text: There is hubbub daily, one states

explanation.surface: Someone complains of a racket every day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'daily' is a noun here: Le Charivari was a French daily paper, which Punch echoed in its subtitle 'The London Charivari'. 'There is' and 'one states' link the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: A charivari is a noisy mock serenade, a din; Le Charivari was also a Paris daily satirical newspaper.

clue.text: Revolutionary fed with scones, it is admitted

indicators.note: Revolutionary says the letters turn over into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A rebel given scones owns up to something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' rearranges FED and SCONES; 'with' and 'it is' link.
explanation.definitionFit: To have confessed is to have owned up or acknowledged guilt.

clue.text: As part of a set, it's left to come later

indicators.note: left means the letters of it are left out

parts.note: en suite means forming a set or matching sequence
the word it, with 's standing for is

explanation.surface: An item from a set is left until afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' drops IT from EN SUITE.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to follow on afterwards, as a result.
